newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Dozens of hostages flee Philippine fighting.
newsitem.headline: Dozens of hostages flee Philippine fighting.

text.p: Nearly 50 hostages seized by Moslem guerrillas dashed to freedom on Thursday during a gun battle between rebels and soldiers in the southern Philippines, the army said.

At least seven people, including a civilian, died in the fighting, which broke out on a country road near Cotabato city after about 150 guerrillas stopped a convoy of passenger buses passing through the area, it said.

The rebels belonging to the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) fled into a coconut plantation and there was no immediate word if they had taken other bus passengers hostage, army spokesman Captain Noel Detoyato said in a radio interview.
But Detoyato said 47 of the hostages had broken free of the guerrillas.
"We ran for our lives when the soldiers arrived and shooting started," said Grace Cadungog, one of the passengers who fled as gunfire broke out.
"One of the gunmen said, 'shoot them', but another one said, 'Don't, let them go'," Cadungog said.
However, MILF political officer Al Mujaheed denied the guerrillas had taken any passengers hostage.

"What happened was that several buses were passing by and we stopped them and asked them not to proceed because they would be in the line of fire between our troops and the government," Mujaheed told Reuters by telephone.
The seven killed in the fighting over the hostages included four guerrillas, two soldiers and one of the bus passengers, the military said.

The military has brought in about 1,500 soldiers and sent in six MG-520 rocket-firing helicopters to back up its 10-day offensive against the rebels. MILF leaders have said the military offensive could scupper peace talks due to restart this weekend.

At least 45 people, mostly rebels, have died and more than 30,000 villagers have fled their homes around towns near Cotabato in more than a week of fighting that began after rebels briefly took over a state-owned oil and gas exploration site on Mindanao island.
The MILF, estimated to have 8,000 armed fighters, is battling for independence for Mindanao, an ancestral Moslem homeland in the predominantly Christian Philippines.
It stayed out of a peace treaty signed late last year by Manila and the mainstream Islamic separatist group, the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
